title: .ensemble/config.yaml
description: The agent team for one project: the agents a calling agent can delegate to, and the LLM backends they can run on. Nothing has a default value: every setting is written, except the two that may be left out because leaving them out means 'not used' (an agent's `prompt` and a backend's `api_key_env`).

llm_backends.description: Model endpoints. The key is the backend's name, which an `opencode` agent's model of type `llm_backend` refers to. Ensemble hands the endpoint and key to the agent's CLI for each run, so they are defined only here. `{}` when there are none.

agents.description: The team. The key is the agent's name, which the calling agent delegates to. The names are yours.

gates.description: Commands a task's work must pass. The key is the gate's name, which a task's `gate` refers to. Defined here so a task names a gate and cannot bring a command of its own. `{}` when there are none.

type.description: per_hour: at most `delegations` runs started in any hour, counted across sessions. Over it, tasks wait and delegations are refused, saying when the next run is allowed.

delegations.description: Runs it may start in any hour.

command.description: A shell command (sh -c) run in the task's working directory after the agent is done. Exit status 0 passes.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the command may run; at the limit it is stopped and the gate fails.

llm_backend.description: How the model is reached. `type` decides which other settings there are.

type.description: openai-compatible-api: any /chat/completions endpoint (llama-server, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, a hosted API).

base_url.description: Where the endpoint is, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key. Keys are never written in this file. Leave it out when the endpoint wants none.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take before the agent's CLI gives up on it.

prompt.description: What this agent is for. Its first line is what the calling agent sees when it lists the team; the whole of it is the agent's system prompt. Keep it short for small local models. Leave it out for an agent with no system prompt.

max_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit for one delegation. At the limit the agent's process is stopped and what it did is returned, marked unfinished.

max_concurrent.description: Most delegations to this agent that run at once in a session, background tasks and blocking calls alike; more wait for a free slot. 1 suits a model server that serves one request at a time.

isolation.description: Where its tasks run. shared: in the project directory. worktree: each task in its own git worktree (.ensemble/worktrees/<id>) on the branch ensemble/<id>, where its work is committed; Ensemble never merges it. Delegations, blocking or in the background, always run in the project.

budget.description: How many runs it may start in an hour: tasks, each gate retry, and delegations, blocking or in the background. `type` decides which other settings there are.

adapter.description: What runs this agent. `type` decides which other settings there are.

type.description: claude-code: the Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`), run headless in the project on your own subscription. It brings its own tools and manages its own context.

model.description: Claude Code's --model: an alias such as sonnet, opus or haiku, or a full model id.

tools.description: Claude Code's own tools this agent may use, passed to --allowedTools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, ..., or a rule such as Bash(git:*). With permission_mode dontAsk anything else is denied. `[Read, Grep, Glob]` is read-only.

permission_mode.description: Claude Code's --permission-mode. dontAsk denies anything not in tools instead of waiting for a person who is not there.

max_turns.description: Most agent turns Claude Code may take for one delegation.

command.description: The claude binary: `claude` if it is on PATH.

type.description: opencode: the OpenCode CLI (`opencode run`), run headless in the project, on one of `llm_backends` or any provider OpenCode is set up for. It brings its own tools and manages its own context.

model.description: Where the model comes from. `type` is `provider` for a model OpenCode is already set up for, or `llm_backend` for one an LLM backend of this config serves.

tools.description: OpenCode permissions this agent is granted: read, glob, grep, list, edit, bash, webfetch, websearch, task, todowrite, ..., or a rule such as bash(git *). Everything else is denied, and OpenCode hides denied tools from the model. `[read, glob, grep, list]` is read-only.

max_steps.description: Most agentic steps OpenCode may take for one delegation; at the limit it reports what it did.

command.description: The opencode binary: `opencode` if it is on PATH.

type.description: provider: a model on a provider OpenCode is already set up for.
llm_backend: a model that one of `llm_backends` serves. Ensemble gives OpenCode that endpoint and its key for the run.

name.description: The model id the endpoint serves, as its /models lists it.

context_window.description: Tokens of context the server really runs the model with (Ollama: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH), so OpenCode knows when to compact the conversation.
